text: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 5Kristopher KnoxOct 7, 2026 We're only a month into the 2026 season, but we've already seen some significant activity on the trade market due to injuries and pressing contract situations. Last week, the New York Giants acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings, a response to losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury. The Pittsburgh Steelers then traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys amid a prolonged contract dispute. According to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, the decision followed another report of back pain from the cornerback, one day after the team listed him as a full participant in practice. While Porter may be the last contract hold-in to be dealt this season, he won't be the last player traded. Injuries continue to mount, and teams are beginning to spiral out of the playoff picture—all five 0-3 teams fell to 0-4 this past week. Here is an updated look at our top 10 trade candidates, ranked by past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, projected availability, and any relevant recent rumors. We'll dive into players that teams should be targeting, project trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, and identify a few logical suitors. 10. Mac Jones, QB, San Francisco 49ers1 of 10AP Photo/John Locher Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick To be clear, Mac Jones remains the best quarterback for teams in need of an immediate starter to target. The 28-year-old went 5-3 with a 97.4 passer rating as the San Francisco 49ers' starter in 2025, and he could steer another playoff-caliber team to the postseason in 2026 if needed. However, the 49ers aren't going to let Jones go for cheap. San Francisco wanted a second-round pick for him in the spring, according to The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt, and the more the Niners believe a Super Bowl run is possible, the less likely they will be to part with their insurance at quarterback. Brock Purdy hasn't been sacked yet this season, but the Niners have experienced enough other early injuries to value proven depth behind him. With quarterbacks like Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels getting closer to a return, there isn't a clear suitor that would pay the hefty price to pry Jones out of San Francisco right now. That could change before November 10, though, and we could see teams that lack a QB plan beyond 2026 enter the mix as well. Potential Suitors: Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets 9. Jadeveon Clowney, Edge, Houston Texans2 of 10AP Photo/Ashley Landis Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick Pass-rushers are always valued around the trade deadline, which is why several reside on our top-10 list. First up is Jadeveon Clowney, who returned late in the offseason to the team that drafted him. The first overall pick in the 2014 draft signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Houston Texans and believed he'd be joining a title contender. However, the Texans have looked like anything but during their 0-4 start to the season. The Texans could still get back in the playoff mix, but they could be prompted to send Clowney to a contender for a strong return—which they should be able to get. Houston could also save $3.3 million in cap space by moving the 33-year-old. Clowney had 8.5 sacks and 22 quarterback pressures with the Dallas Cowboys last season. He returned from a two-game absence due to a bone bruise in his knee and recorded a half-sack against Dallas in Week 4. In two games this season, Clowney has recorded 1.5 sacks and four QB pressures. He should interest most teams in need of pass-rushing help this season. Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Dallas Cowboys 8. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers3 of 10AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick While the demand for a fill-in starter may be dwindling, the market for a backup QB may be heating up. The Washington Commanders may be close to having Daniels back, but backup Marcus Mariota is now dealing with an MCL injury. While Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking at Easton Stick behind undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. An increased backup-QB market could benefit the Pittsburgh Steelers, who were reportedly open to moving Mason Rudolph at the start of the season, according to Jason La Canfora of Casino.org. Rudolph, who has 20 career starts (including playoffs), is one of the league's better backups. He could also be viewed as expendable, as Pittsburgh has Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind Aaron Rodgers. Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, Arizona Cardinals4 of 10AP Photo/Adam Hunger Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick The Arizona Cardinals have lost three straight and are looking like a team that may soon begin playing for 2027 and beyond. Arizona's quarterback of the future probably isn't on the current roster, though the Cardinals have several promising offensive pieces they can eventually put around him. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love all project as long-term building blocks, though 2024 first-round pick Marvin Harrison Jr. may not. Harrison was widely viewed as a "can't-miss" prospect when the Cardinals drafted him fourth overall. However, he has fallen behind in Arizona's offensive game plan and could probably use a change of scenery. Unfortunately, it appears that Harrison's trade value is at an all-time low—some teams believe he may not command more than a Day-3 pick, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The Cardinals probably won't let Harrison go for that low a price, but it feels like a team willing to bet on his upside could snag him before the deadline. Potential Suitors: Indianapolis Colts, Kansas City Chiefs 6. Solomon Thomas, DL, Tennessee Titans5 of 10AP Photo/Stew Milne Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 7th-Round Draft Pick Like the Texans, the Tennessee Titans are sitting at 0-4 and staring down a lost season. The AFC South rivals face one another in Week 5, giving both a chance to secure their first win. However, Tennessee feels much further away from turning things around than Houston does. Let's not forget that the Texans rebounded from a 0-3 start last year and still made the postseason. The Titans went 3-14 in each of the past two campaigns. Tennessee will likely use the rest of 2026 to evaluate quarterback Cam Ward and determine whether it should consider replacing him with a top 2027 prospect. Veteran players who won't contribute toward that goal should be viewed as expendable. The Titans traded for defensive lineman Solomon Thomas in the offseason, reuniting him with head coach Robert Saleh. While Thomas has appeared in all four games this season, he has played just 25 percent of the defensive snaps. Thomas, who will be a free agent in 2027, has little long-term value to the Titans. However, he could bolster a contender's defensive line. Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Cleveland Browns 5. Walker Little, OT, Jacksonville Jaguars6 of 10AP PhotoPhelan M. Ebenhack Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick and/or Veteran Defender The Jacksonville Jaguars moved to 3-1 on Saturday, and they certainly aren't going to sell off pieces the way that the league's winless teams might. However, they have a high-priced backup in Walker Little who could draw significant interest in the wake of more offensive tackle injuries. The Cardinals, for example, recently placed starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. on injured reserve with a torn bicep. He'll miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Little was a starter for the Jaguars before losing his job at left tackle to Cole Van Lanen. He has appeared in all four games this season but has played just 24 offensive snaps and 21 snaps on special teams. With 39 starts on his resume, Little should bring a moderate return on the trade market. Jacksonville would also save $11.4 million in cap space by moving him. Potential Suitors: Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers 4. Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers7 of 10AP Photo Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick Injuries continue to mount at running back across the NFL. Jadarian Price, Tank Bigsby, and Travis Etienne Jr. have all recently landed on injured reserve, and Miami Dolphins starter De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL. The Buccaneers, who are sitting at 0-4 with an undrafted rookie at quarterback, could cash in on the run of injuries by moving backup Kenneth Gainwell. Gainwell signed a two-year, $14 million deal in the offseason to back up Bucs starter Bucky Irving. The Buccaneers would save just $2 million in 2026 cap space by trading the 27-year-old, but they could clear his 2027 $7 million cap hit from the books while getting a reasonable return. While Gainwell did score his first touchdown for Tampa in Week 4, he has still logged a mere 21 touches through four weeks. However, he racked up 187 touches, 1,023 scrimmage yards, and eight touchdowns with the Steelers last season. At this point in the season, Gainwell would boost the backfield depth of multiple teams. Potential Suitors: Philadelphia Eagles, Seattle Seahawks 3. Josh Uche, Edge, Miami Dolphins8 of 10AP Photo/Doug Murray Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick The Dolphins haven't really hidden the fact that they're playing for the future in 2026. They gambled on quarterback Malik Willis in free agency, but they dumped most of their noteworthy veterans during the offseason. The Dolphins do have some nice young pieces on their roster and just played a very competitive game against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. However, they're still sitting at 0-4 and are highly unlikely to get in the AFC East race at any point this season. While Miami may not be interested in parting with any more potential long-term building blocks—like 23-year-old edge-defender Chop Robinson—it should be willing to move pass-rusher Josh Uche. The 28-year-old has been a veteran leader early in the season but is only playing on a one-year deal. Uche recorded his first sack of the season against Minnesota, and he has logged four QB pressures and 17 total tackles through four weeks. He should be very attractive to teams that either lack edge-rushing depth or have lost it to injury during the first month of the season. Potential Suitors: New York Giants, Philadelphia Eagles 2. Jerry Jeudy, WR, Cleveland Browns9 of 10AP Photo/Gary McCullough Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick The Cleveland Browns moved to 3-1 with a win over the Steelers in Week 4. During their latest victory, they got a handful of clutch catches from veteran receiver Jerry Jeudy. According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com, the Browns aren't interested in trading the 27-year-old right now. However, Cabot's report clashes with that of ESPN insider Adam Schefter. "Jeudy is being squeezed out. He could be had by the trade deadline," Schefter told NFL Sunday Countdown (beginning around the 46-second mark). Jeudy is being "squeezed out" of the offense by promising rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, who have quickly emerged as go-to targets. While Jeudy did play a role in Cleveland's latest win, he's caught just five of eight targets for 62 yards on the season. A 1,200-yard receiver and a Pro Bowler in 2024, Jeudy should interest receiver-needy teams, as should his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million. Potential Suitors: Kansas City Chiefs, Philadelphia Eagles 1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers10 of 10AP Photo/Kyusung Gong Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick The Los Angeles Chargers made the playoffs in their first two years under head coach Jim Harbaugh, and most viewed them as 2026 playoff contenders. However, the Chargers are now among the league's winless teams and are potentially looking at a lost season. This isn't the sort of situation Khalil Mack believed he was joining when he re-signed on a one-year, $18 million deal this offseason. Mack has not been part of the disappointment in Los Angeles, as he's off to a very strong start to the season. He's already logged 14 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, and eight quarterback pressures. The Chargers won't be eager to move Mack as long as they believe they can rebound. If they believe their season is lost, however, they could save $8 million in cap space by moving him. They could also expect a strong return for the 35-year-old, who has the potential to push a playoff-caliber defense into championship territory. Stephen A. Smith Apologizes for Lane Johnson Retirement Comments on Mental HealthTimothy RappOct 7, 2026ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith apologized Wednesday for his criticism of Lane Johnson's decision to retire this week after suggesting that the Philadelphia Eagles' tackle retired due to the team's struggles this season rather than the "personal and family priorities" and "mental health" reasons Johnson cited.Smith claimed that people "misconstrued me making light of mental health, I would never do that."TOP NEWSLane Johnson Retirement Post🦅Bleacher Report1dMark Ingram's Fantasy Post 😭Bleacher Report2dRavens Trade for Eagles Pro Bowl OL 🚨Bleacher Report2hJohnson said in his retirement post that he "deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season," hence his decision not to retire before the season. Ultimately, however, he said that his priorities changed after a period of "reflection."Across both the NFL and within Philadelphia, the response was one of understanding regarding his decision and gratitude for his 14 years with the Eagles.The 36-year-old is a future Hall of Famer and one of the best right tackles in NFL history. He was a two-time champion, six-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro, and during his career the Eagles were a far more successful team with him on the field than off."I've said it before: First-ballot Hall of Famer," general manager Howie Roseman said of Johnson. "... Huge, big part of our success. Just someone you never took for granted every day. Practice, games—just felt totally honored that he was our right tackle for as long as he was. And the relationship, just having him around, and the relationship we had through all those years and through the things we had to go through with our team and what was going on with all of us personally, we'll miss him, and just very appreciative of him and his contributions to our success."The Eagles have had quite the turnover at offensive line this season. Longtime offensive-line coach and run-game coordinator Jeff Stoutland left his post before the season as the team shifted to a new running scheme under offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Three-time Pro Bowler Landon Dickerson is on injured reserve with a knee injury, and after struggling with injuries last season, there are questions about his future. Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Tuesday alongside a 2027 seventh-rounder for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder after struggling with the move from center to guard this season. Philly's offensive line, once one of the best units in the NFL, has struggled the past two seasons. Losing Johnson most certainly won't help, but he has the right to leave on his own terms, however abrupt the decision may have felt from the outside. 01:06 Falcons May Have Figured It Out 🗣️TOP NEWSLane Johnson Retirement Post🦅Bleacher Report1dMark Ingram's Fantasy Post 😭Bleacher Report2dRavens Trade for Eagles Pro Bowl OL 🚨Bleacher Report2hEagles reveal surprising London travel plansBleacher Report1dSaquon Considered Week-to-WeekBleacher Report1dTRENDING ON B/RBleacher Report•4hTop 99 NFL rookie this seasoncnnBleacher Report•5h5 NFL Players Getting Trade BuzzBleacher Report•3h🚨Dana Altman RetiringOregon HC stepping down immediately; ex-DePaul HC Tony Stubblefield to be interimBleacher Report•2hDak to Stroud: Get Some Wins 💯Postgame convo between QBs goes viralBleacher Report•2h76ers HC Addresses Bron-Embiid RumorsBleacher Report•2hOBJ Takes McCarthy's Number 9️⃣web headlinesBleacher Report•3hEagles Loading Up on Picks 🛒webBleacher Report•9hNew Rankings After 1st Week 📊webBleacher Report•5hColts Owner Defends ApproachCarlie Irsay-Gordon explains viral clips of taking notes on sidelines

MLB Playoff Divisional Round Overreactions to Dodgers vs. Braves, Rays vs. Yankees and Every GameKerry MillerOct 7, 2026 When the summer doldrums start to wear you down as a baseball fan, dreaming about days like these can quickly put that pep back in your step. Four postseason games, back-to-back-to-back-to-back. All of them are potential elimination games, no less. And we've celebrated the occasion with one rapid (over)reaction for each of the eight teams in action. Cleveland Guardians: They Done Woke Up J-Ram1 of 8Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images For most of this season, José Ramírez simply wasn't the J-Ram we've come to know and love. Even before suffering that broken hamate in mid-June, he was only on pace for 22 home runs and 74 RBI, both of which would have been his worst (non-2020) totals since 2016. But he really was not the same after his return to the lineup. In his last 52 regular-season games, Ramírez hit just two home runs and posted a .593 OPS. And in the first two postseason games against the White Sox, he went 0-for-6 with two walks and three strikeouts. At long last, though, the proverbial light may have come back on. J-Ram went 2-for-4 with a double, a triple, a stolen base and a walk in Wednesday's 9-3 win over Chicago. Even his unsuccessful plate appearances were impressive. The lineout in the first inning was scalded at 107.9 MPH with an expected batting average of .830. It just happened to find Randal Grichuk's glove. He also worked the count full before popping out in the seventh inning. But it was the double-stolen base-run scored on a grounder sequence in the fifth inning that felt like the J-Ram of yore. And the two-run triple in the eighth made it feel like more than a flash in the pan. If he's back—with Parker Messick pitching Thursday and Gavin Williams gearing up for Game 5—Cleveland might storm back from a 2-0 deficit. (Also, three cheers to Foster Griffin, who struck out seven of the 11 batters he faced to get the win. He had a 5.19 ERA after relocating from Washington at the trade deadline, but that was huge.) Chicago White Sox: The Bullpen Shtick Has Finally Imploded2 of 8Jessie Alcheh/Major League Baseball via Getty Images In winning their first four postseason games, the Chicago White Sox's MVP was the entire bullpen. Of the total 36 innings pitched in those victories, the bullpen was responsible for 26.0, doing so with a 1.04 ERA, 0.69 WHIP and 10.4 K/9. It was as if they all of a sudden had nine Josh Haders out there. (Houston's Hader finished the year with a 1.01 ERA, 0.76 WHIP and 11.1 K/9 in his 44.2 innings of dominance.) But after Sean Newcomb gave them two scoreless innings in starting Game 3, the wheels came all the way off. Starting with Bryan Hudson, the subsequent six White Sox pitchers took turns getting smoked to the tune of 10 hits, 10 walks and nine earned runs as the Guardians lived to see another day. Notably, Jordan Hicks and Grant Taylor played no part in that implosion. The former has gone 10.1 scoreless innings with 18 strikeouts since Labor Day, while the latter has been quietly one of MLB's most dominant relievers since July 4. All the same, the dam may have broken on Wednesday. A very limited supply of reliable pitching was everyone's concern about the White Sox heading into the postseason, and it finally reared its ugly head in Game 3. Can they reel it back in on Thursday, presumably with Erick Fedde and Taylor each pitching multiple innings? Los Angeles Dodgers: There Is No Achilles' Heel3 of 8Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Less than one month ago, the thought of Edwin Díaz pitching in anything close to a high-leverage situation for the Dodgers was inconceivable. In 16 appearances across two trips to the IL, he posted a 11.85 ERA and blew four of his last seven save chances. But something clicked during his last rehab assignment. Over his final five regular-season appearances, he struck out nine of 17 batters faced while allowing just two baserunners. And after pitching a flawless sixth inning in Game 2, Dave Roberts had seen enough to put him back in the closer role for Games 3 and 4. He locked them both down, not even allowing a baserunner in the series clincher. Meanwhile, the hero in both Games 3 and 4 came out of the 9-hole in the lineup. After not even getting a plate appearance in Game 1 or Game 2, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning in Game 3 to break a scoreless tie, ultimately driving in the winning run. On Wednesday night, Andy Pages delivered a massive two-out, two-run single that put the Dodgers ahead for good. Of course, with this loaded roster, the 9-hole has never been much of a hole. During the regular season, they had an MLB-best .259 batting average from that bottom spot in the order. But those two games in Atlanta were a sobering reminder that there are no easy outs when facing the twice-reigning champs. TOP NEWSMLB Division Series Action 🍿Bleacher Report1hEvery Playoff Team's October X-Factor ❌Bleacher Report2dUpdated MLB Postseason Bracket 📋Bleacher Report4hAtlanta Braves: It Might Be Time to Trade Ronald Acuña Jr.4 of 8Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Ronald Acuña Jr. is a five-time All-Star and a three-time Silver Slugger. He was the NL Rookie of the Year in 2018 and the NL MVP in 2023. When he's at his best, not many who have ever played the game have been better. But he sure has been a ghost in October for a while now. Dating back to Game 2 of the 2020 NLDS against Miami, Acuña has gone 14-for-84 (.167 AVG) with 24 strikeouts, zero home runs and just one RBI in 24 games played. The idea of Atlanta trading away its final two years of team control on Acuña would have been considered blasphemy just a few days ago. Braves fans certainly sang his praises when he played a massive role in keeping the Phillies at bay in the first half of September. But here at the end of his third consecutive injury-plagued season, the fans sure seem to have had enough of his inability to deliver when they need him the most, going 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position this postseason. We'll leave the "Where would he go?" and "How much could they get?" speculations for another day, but it does feel like the Braves need to do something drastic to shake things up after yet another early flameout in October. Tampa Bay Rays: Welcome to the Victor Mesa Jr. Show5 of 8Michael Urakami/Major League Baseball via Getty Images For most of the regular season, I was reluctant to believe the Tampa Bay Rays could win the World Series. It's not because of their payroll, nor the fact that they have never won it all before. Rather, it's because, for most of the season, it felt like they could get swept in a series if Junior Caminero and/or Yandy Díaz went through a cold spell. So much of this offense depended on that dynamic duo in the first half of the year. Chandler Simpson really started to heat up in July, though. They traded for Liam Hicks in August, bolstering a problematic catcher spot in the lineup. But the final, biggest nudge that pushed the Rays into Serious Contender-ville came when Victor Mesa Jr. caught fire in September. The rookie had a 1.015 OPS in the final month of the regular season, blossoming into a near-daily fixture in the lineup. And after catching that controversial Spencer Jones fly ball off the catwalk early in Game 2 in Tampa Bay, Mesa delivered the 401-foot haymaker of a two-run home run off Max Fried in the sixth inning. Fried had allowed just four home runs during the regular season. His 0.32 HR/9 rate was the lowest among pitchers in a season with at least 100 innings pitched since 2014. He hadn't allowed a single home run to a left-handed hitter all season. That's how legends are born, though. And Mesa's postseason legend might just be getting started. New York Yankees: Fire. Aaron. Boone.6 of 8Mary DeCicco/Major League Baseball via Getty Images Aaron Boone isn't to blame for Aaron Judge's postseason absence. It's not Aaron Boone's fault that the Yankees couldn't field their way out of a paper bag in Game 2 of this series against the Rays. It's not Aaron Boone's fault that Ryan Vilade's deep fly ball traveled just beyond Spencer Jones' outstretched glove, nor that Anthony Volpe's deep fly ball a few innings later traveled only far enough for a fan-interference decision heard 'round the world. It's not Aaron Boone's fault that Max Fried picked the worst possible moment to allow his first home run to a left-handed hitter (Victor Mesa Jr.) since August 2025, more than 30 starts ago. And we know this because nothing ever seems to be Aaron Boone's fault. How can the Yankees justify keeping him once again after yet another embarrassing postseason exit? He is now 27-30 in the postseason in his nine-year managerial career, and has overseen more than 50 percent of what is now a 17-year drought without a World Series title. On the one hand, many MLB fan bases would do anything to experience 57 postseason games in less than a decade. On the other hand, six-ish postseason games per year is pretty much the bare minimum when you're the Damn Yankees. George Steinbrenner would've fired Boone at least four times by now. And if Hal Steinbrenner doesn't do it now, he might as well put out a public statement that simply making the playoffs (while turning a profit) is the new Yankee Way. Milwaukee Brewers: We'll Be Talking About "The Garrett Mitchell Game" for Years7 of 8Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images For years, Milwaukee Brewers fans had been wondering what Garrett Mitchell could do at full strength. After going 20th overall in the 2020 draft, his "games played" count through his first half-decade in the pros was 64, 96, 27, 83 and 29, suffering one injury after another. At long last, though, he had a healthy season in 2026, becoming Milwaukee's primary center fielder behind the strength of his blistering speed. And in the series-clinching victory over the Padres, he was everywhere. It was Mitchell's single up the middle in the third inning that produced the first run of the night. It was Mitchell's leadoff triple in the fifth inning that set the table for Jackson Chourio's game-winning RBI. And it was Mitchell's home run robbery of Manny Machado in the eighth inning that saved the game while evoking memories of Adam Jones' catch in the 2017 World Baseball Classic. Previously, "The Garrett Mitchell Game" was Game 2 in the 2024 wild card round against the Mets, when his two-run home run broke an eighth inning tie and brought the Brewers a season-saving victory. That was one moment, though, and quickly forgotten when they collapsed the following night. This was his game, setting up the NLCS rematch with the Dodgers. Does he have a few more tricks up his sleeve? San Diego Padres: Never Going to Get Over the Hump8 of 8Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images The San Diego Padres entered the NLDS hotter than a thousand suns. They won 17 of their final 20 regular season games, leading the majors in runs scored during that time. They also breezed through the wild card round against the Cubs, shutting down the best offense in baseball by a combined score of 12-1. But as they always eventually do, they ran out of gas in painstaking fashion. With help from the roof at American Family Field, they blew an early 2-0 lead in losing Game 1. In Game 2, the greatest closer in all the land may or may not have been tipping his pitches for another heartbreaking loss. And after clawing back to take Game 3, Manny Machado's would-be game-tying home run in Game 4 wasn't meant to be, as this scorching hot offense was extinguished in a 3-1 loss. It's becoming an all-too-familiar tale in San Diego. They scored just one run in each of their losses in last year's wild card round. They blew a 2-1 series lead in the 2024 NLDS by failing to score for 24 consecutive innings. And let's not even talk about Josh Hader's availability with two innings remaining in the 2022 NLCS. Despite Machado, Fernando Tatis Jr., Xander Bogaerts and more, it's just never enough for a team that is starting to feel destined to never win a World Series. For now, they're tied with the Brewers as the longest-existing franchises to have never won it all. We'll see in a few weeks' time whether that's still the case. 01:18 Dodgers Advance to 3rd-Straight NLCS 🔵TOP NEWSMLB Division Series Action 🍿Bleacher Report1hEvery Playoff Team's October X-Factor ❌Bleacher Report2dUpdated MLB Postseason Bracket 📋Bleacher Report4hSchlittler: We Didn't Show Up 🫥Bleacher Report1dRays Hang On vs. Yankees 🤏Bleacher Report2hTRENDING ON B/RBleacher Report•2hMLB Lays Out Lockout PlansNew details emerge on 34-page memo with team owners and high-ranking execs (The Athletic)Bleacher Report•9hPeyton Manning's Son's CFB Offers Bleacher Report•6hKOC Contacted OBJ After Release ☎️Bleacher Report•9hBroadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumorcnnBleacher Report•10hStephen A. Aaron Boone Describes 'Broken' Clubhouse, Ripped by Fans as Yankees Swept Out of MLB PlayoffsTimothy RappOct 7, 2026The New York Yankees were swept in the ALDS, losing 4-3 to the Tampa Bay Rays during Wednesday's Game 3.Manager Aaron Boone was feeling the effects:TOP NEWSMLB Lays Out Lockout PlansBleacher Report41mDodgers Clinch NLCS ReturnBleacher Report3hPredicting the Outcome for Each Team's Top Free Agent 🔮Bleacher Report14hHe won't be getting much sympathy from Yankees' fans, however—Boone is not a popular man in the Big Apple at the moment:"Those are conversations for another day," Boone told reporters Wednesday night when asked about his job security, which might be true for himself but certainly wasn't true among Yankees' fans. In his nine seasons as Yankees' manager the team has yet to win a World Series title and only played in the Fall Classic once (2024). The Bronx Bombers have made the playoffs in eight of Boone's nine seasons but only advanced past the ALDS three times.In some markets, that level of consistency would represent a memorable period. But given the Yankees' historical pedigree—and astronomical payroll, even if it no longer tops the sport—expectations are much higher. A Representative APR is a financial service concept in the United Kingdom and the European Union in which credit or loan interest rates quoted through advertising media are required to take into account all charges associated with a product, in addition to the interest rate. History For years, financial services companies in the United Kingdom had been required to quote an Annual Percentage Rate (APR) in any credit terms or advertisements. Up until 2010, all businesses had to comply with the UK Consumer Credit ( ) Regulations 2004 (2004 Regulations). However, all European Union member states adopted a new Directive in April 2008. This was implemented in the UK by the Consumer Credit (EU Directive) Regulations 2010, which came into force for all UK companies on 1 February 2011. While the Directive is similar to the existing policies adopted in the UK, there are a couple of major changes. One of the most important of these is introduction of a ‘Representative APR’. What the rules say The Department for Business, Skills and Innovation (BSI) is clear on what the new Directive means for financial services providers and consumers in the UK. The BSI states: “If an advertisement includes an interest rate or any amount relating to the cost of credit, it must also include a representative example. This must contain certain standard information including a representative APR. The example must be clear and concise and must be more prominent than the information that triggered the inclusion of the example.” Products the rules apply to The new Directive applies to advertisements and credit agreements for all loans to consumers under £60,260 excluding: agreements secured on land business loans (certified) investments regulated by the FSA Definition of ‘representative APR’ The APR for financial services products often varies from customer to customer. This is particularly true if loan or credit card rates are determined by an individual's income or credit rating. In addition, the problem with the current way of working out an APR is that it often doesn't take into account certain fees, such as credit card balance transfer fees or annual charges. So, in instances where the APR for a financial product can vary, the APR that is stated on an advertisement must represent the business that the financial services provider expects to come from that advert. A representative APR will also take into account other charges associated with the product (in addition to the interest rate) and will be displayed within the Representative Example. A company works out its ‘typical’ APR by taking into account past business that has arisen from advertising similar products, ideally over the previous 12 months. The Financial Services Authority (FSA) Archived 2009-02-27 at the Wayback Machine suggests to companies that they “list the APRs your customers have paid over the past 12 months. The representative APR you state in your advert should not be less than the APR paid by at least 66% of consumers on the list.” However, from 1 February 2011, this calculation changed. The BSI reports that: “The Representative APR must reflect at least 51% of business expected to result from the advertisement. The standard information must be representative of agreements to which the Representative APR applies.” A representative APR will be based on a credit limit of £1,200 (unless known to be lower). Additional services and security Another subtle but important change to the rules now make it essential for financial services providers to display, in prominent text, whether there are any obligations on a consumer to enter into another contract (for example, if you have to take compulsory insurance products with a mortgage loan). In this situation, the cost must be shown with: no less prominence than standard information the representative APR The nature of any security must also be specified. References
